questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding the mammary glands?

options.text: It is a modified sweat gland
It lies on the deep pectoral fascia
It is supplied by internal thoracic artery
Nipple is supplied by the 6th intercostal nerve

questions.correctAnswerText: Nipple is supplied by the 6th intercostal nerve
questions.explanation: The nipple is supplied by the anterior branch of the lateral cutaneous branch of T4 (4th intercostal nerve), so the statement that it is supplied by the 6th intercostal nerve is incorrect. The breast is innervated by anterior and lateral branches of the 4th to 6th intercostal nerves (sensory and sympathetic efferent). The mammary gland is a modified sweat gland lying on the deep pectoral fascia over pectoralis major. It receives blood from the internal thoracic artery, lateral thoracic artery and lateral branches of posterior intercostal arteries.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: After a detailed evaluation, a woman is found to have a breast lump extending into the axillary tail of Spence. Through which of the following foramina does the affected structure pass?
questions.explanation: The axillary tail of Spence is the axillary process of the mammary gland. It passes through the foramen of Langer. The foramen of Langer is an opening in the deep fascia through which the superolateral quadrant is prolonged toward the axilla. It lies along the inferolateral edge of pectoralis major and may extend through the deep fascia up to the apex of the axilla.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following does not provide direct blood supply to the breast tissue?
questions.explanation: The direct blood supply of the breast does not include the axillary artery itself. Major sources shown in the source table are lateral thoracic artery to the lateral breast; medial mammary branches of the internal thoracic artery to the medial breast; pectoral branches of thoracoacromial and superior thoracic arteries to the superior breast; and 2nd-4th posterior intercostal arteries to the base. The veins generally correspond with the arteries and drain into axillary and internal thoracic veins. The source notes that the left internal mammary (internal thoracic) artery is preferred for coronary artery bypass grafting because it has superior short- and long-term patency compared with saphenous-vein grafts.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statement about breast tissue is false?

options.text: Fibrous stroma is absent beneath the areola
Alveolar epithelium is columnar in the resting phase
15-20 lactiferous ducts open in the nipple
Myoepitheliocytes facilitates the passage of the milk along the ducts

questions.correctAnswerText: Alveolar epithelium is columnar in the resting phase
questions.explanation: Alveolar epithelium is cuboidal in the resting phase and columnar during lactation, so the statement that it is columnar in the resting phase is false. Fibrous stroma forms septa (suspensory ligaments of Cooper) anchoring skin and gland to pectoral fascia; it forms the major part of the gland but is absent beneath the areola and nipple. During development, thoracic ectodermal ingrowths form 15-20 solid buds that canalize into lactiferous ducts and secretory alveoli. Contraction of myoepitheliocytes facilitates passage of milk along the ducts. The 15-20 lactiferous ducts converge toward the nipple and form lactiferous sinuses.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The secretion of breast milk is ________
questions.explanation: Mammary gland cells secrete milk protein (casein) by merocrine secretion, while milk lipid is secreted by apocrine secretion. Therefore breast-milk secretion combines apocrine and merocrine mechanisms. The source summarizes gland secretion types: merocrine - vesicles fuse with plasma membrane and release their contents; apocrine - the apical portion of the cell is pinched off for secretion (examples include milk fat, atypical sweat glands and ceruminous glands); holocrine - the entire gland cell disintegrates to liberate secretion (e.g., sebaceous glands). Eccrine sweat glands were formerly classified as eccrine but are now placed under merocrine.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 58-year-old woman was diagnosed with a malignant tumor in the superolateral quadrant of the breast. A blue dye was injected to map the sentinel lymph node for evaluation of metastasis. Which of the following lymph nodes would most likely be removed for biopsy?
questions.explanation: Lymphatics from the upper outer quadrant of the breast drain first into the anterior axillary lymph nodes, which therefore function as sentinel nodes in this setting. A sentinel node is the first lymph node receiving lymphatic drainage from a tumor and may be removed during surgery for histopathological assessment of metastasis. Axillary nodes receive more than 75% of breast lymph. The source also classifies axillary nodes relative to pectoralis minor: Level 1 (low nodes) below pectoralis minor; Level 2 (middle nodes) behind the muscle; Level 3 (apical/upper nodes) between the upper border of pectoralis minor and lower border of clavicle. Nodes between pectoralis major and minor are interpectoral (Rotter's) nodes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 40-year-old woman with breast cancer presents to the OPD with the given finding on her right breast. What is the likely cause of this finding?

options.text: Infiltration of the ligament of Cooper

questions.explanation: The image shows the peau d'orange appearance of the breast. It occurs due to blockade of sub-dermal lymphatics and is one of the most conspicuous signs of breast cancer. Obstruction of lymphatic drainage produces edema of the breast, but the swollen skin remains tethered to the ligaments of Cooper; the sweat-gland and hair-follicle openings are pulled inward, producing the typical orange-peel appearance.
